title_vi: Khóa bi quan và khóa lạc quan: hai người cùng mua vé cuối

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a partial clone of the source repository; git hash-object of the retrieved body matches the source-map blob. No source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Mức cô lập REPEATABLE READ cũng chặn mất cập nhật, như dòng cuối của thử nghiệm.
Bài về các loại khóa của cơ sở dữ liệu đi sâu hơn vào khóa hàng và khóa bảng.

claims.evidence: PostgreSQL 16 ref/select.sgml (The Locking Clause) and mvcc.sgml (row-level locks, Repeatable Read update conflicts, deadlocks) were read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres; the three-way ticket experiment, NOWAIT and Repeatable Read results come from the author's own run on PostgreSQL 16.15 on 2026-10-18 (psycopg 3, two connections).

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: FOR UPDATE locks the selected rows as though for update, so other transactions that try to update, delete or lock them block until the current transaction ends; NOWAIT reports an error instead of waiting and SKIP LOCKED skips rows that cannot be locked.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: A Repeatable Read transaction that tries to update a row changed by a transaction committed after it began fails with 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update', and the application should retry the whole transaction.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: PostgreSQL detects deadlocks and aborts one of the transactions; the best defence is to acquire locks on multiple objects in a consistent order.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at REL_16_STABLE commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: Measured on PostgreSQL 16.15 with one ticket left: without locking both buyers sold; with SELECT FOR UPDATE the second buyer waited 1.0 s (the first held the lock for 1 s) and then saw 0 and refused; with a version column one UPDATE changed 1 row and the other 0 rows (final version 2); FOR UPDATE NOWAIT failed at once with 'could not obtain lock on row in relation'; under REPEATABLE READ the second writer got 'could not serialize access due to concurrent update'.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured this on 2026-10-18; not repeated on other versions.

claims.claim_vi: The source states: Pessimistic locking assumes conflicts and locks before changes; optimistic locking checks for conflicts at commit and rolls back; best practices include short locks, row-level granularity and retry logic. The lesson does not adopt the rollback wording: a version-checked UPDATE changes 0 rows and the application must notice it (see source_deviations).

design_notes_vi: Một khung lỗi mất cập nhật, hai khung cho hai cách khóa với cùng ví dụ vé cuối, một khung chọn cách. Số trong hình lấy từ thử nghiệm riêng.
source_deviations: The source says optimistic locking rolls the operation back on conflict; the lesson shows that a version-checked UPDATE simply changes 0 rows and the application must notice it.
The source ranks pessimistic locking as better for data integrity; the lesson shows that both correct methods sell one ticket and differ in waiting versus retrying.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
